remedies.title: Ask to be put back on the roll with Form 6
remedies.plain: If your name was left off the draft or the final roll, fill in Form 6, the application to be added to the roll. During the claims and objections period of the revision it goes with the declaration attached to it for the revision. Once the revision is over in your state you can still apply at any time under continuous updation, on the ordinary Form 6 of the 1960 Rules. Form 6A is for Indian citizens living abroad, and Form 8 is for a change of address or a mistake in your own entry.
steps: Get Form 6 from your booth level officer (BLO), the registration officer's office, voters.eci.gov.in or the ECINet app.
During the revision, attach the declaration that goes with Form 6 for the revision.
Hand it to the BLO or the registration officer, or file it online, and keep the reference number.
Apply well before an election is called. No name can be added after the last date for nominations until that election is over.
Use Form 8 if you moved house, within the state or from another state, or if your entry has a mistake. Use Form 6A if you live abroad on an Indian passport.

remedies.title: Objections and the hearing before any deletion
remedies.plain: Form 7 is the form for objecting to a name on the roll, or to a name proposed to be added. When someone objects to your name, the registration officer has to send you a notice and hear you before deciding. Before striking off a name on the ground that the person has moved away or is not entitled to be on the roll, the officer has to give that person a reasonable chance to be heard. In the revision no entry could be deleted from the draft without an inquiry and a fair chance to be heard, followed by a written order with reasons. If you get a notice, go to the hearing or send the documents asked for, and ask for the order in writing.
steps: Check the lists of claims and objections the registration officer puts up on the notice board and the Chief Electoral Officer's website.
If someone has objected to your name, you should get a notice with the date, time and place of the hearing.
Attend in person or through someone you authorise where that is allowed, and take your documents.
Ask for the registration officer's decision in writing. You need it for an appeal.

sources.doc: ECI SIR Order No. 23/2025-ERS (Vol.II) of 24.06.2025, para 14, as published by CEO Kerala
sources.quote: The ERO/AERO shall not delete any entry from the draft roll without conducting an inquiry and giving a fair and reasonable opportunity to the persons concerned whose name has appeared in the draft roll.

remedies.title: Appeal to the District Magistrate, then to the Chief Electoral Officer
remedies.plain: If the registration officer's decision goes against you, you can appeal to the District Magistrate under section 24 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950. If the District Magistrate's order also goes against you, a second appeal lies to the state's Chief Electoral Officer. The Commission's revision order kept both appeals and gave 30 days from the District Magistrate's order for the second. The Chief Electoral Officer of Goa, in the note on its final roll, gave 15 days from the registration officer's decision for the first.
steps: Get a copy of the registration officer's order.
Write a short appeal to the District Magistrate, signed by you, with the order attached, within 15 days of the registration officer's decision.
If it is turned down, appeal to the Chief Electoral Officer within 30 days of the District Magistrate's order.
Keep copies and receipts of everything you hand in.

sources.doc: Representation of the People Act, 1950, section 24, copy published by the High Court of Tripura
sources.quote: An appeal shall lie within such time and in suc h manner as may be prescribed— (a) to the district magistrate or additional district magistr ate or executive magistrate or district collector or an officer of equivalent rank , from any order of the electoral registration officer under section 22 or section 23 ... ( b) to the chief electoral officer, from any order of the district magistrate or the additional district magistrate under clause ( a)

remedies.title: The 1950 helpline, complaints, and the drive to find those left off
remedies.plain: You can call the voter helpline on 1950, or the national toll-free number 1800-11-1950 from 8 am to 8 pm, and every complaint is logged on the National Grievance Service Portal. The ECINet app has a Book-a-Call with BLO feature, and complaints can also be emailed to complaints@eci.gov.in. After the revision, the Commission ordered BLOs to compare the roll from before the revision with the present one, visit those missing, and help anyone still eligible fill in Form 6. The lists are to be shared with the parties' booth agents, and booth level camps are to be held. Special camps may also be held for people in night shelters and labour colonies and for the homeless.
steps: Call 1950, or 1800-11-1950, and note the complaint number.
Use Book-a-Call with BLO on the ECINet app to ask your BLO to visit.
If a BLO visits during the drive, fill in Form 6 then and there if you are eligible.
Look for booth level camps in your area, and special camps if you live in a night shelter or labour colony.

sources.doc: ECI press release, PIB, 29.10.2025
sources.quote: It operates daily from 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM through toll-free number 1800-11-1950 .

sources.doc: ECI press release, PIB, 29.10.2025
sources.quote: All complaints and queries are recorded and tracked through the National Grievance Service Portal (NGSP 2.0). Additionally, ECI has also launched ‘Book-a-Call with BLO’ facility using which citizens can directly contact their respective Booth Level Officer (BLO) through the feature available on the ECINET platform.

remedies.title: Free legal help from the legal services authorities
remedies.plain: Under section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, women, children, members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, people with disabilities, industrial workers, victims of disaster and people below an income limit set by each state can get free legal help. Legal services include advice and help before any authority, so they can cover a claim, a hearing or an appeal about the roll. Ask at the District Legal Services Authority at the district court, or call the NALSA helpline on 15100. In Bihar in September 2025 the Supreme Court had the legal services authorities send para-legal volunteers to help voters file claims and objections online.
steps: Call 15100 or visit the District Legal Services Authority office at the district court.
Say that your name was left off the roll and what stage you are at (claim, hearing or appeal).
Take the notice or order you received and any documents you have.
Ask for a para-legal volunteer or panel lawyer to help you fill in the form or the appeal.

These Authorities were required to depute and notify para-legal volunteers, along with their names and mobile numbers, who would assist individual voters or political parties in submitting claims, objections, and corrections through the online process.

remedies.title: What the Supreme Court's orders give an elector
remedies.plain: In Bihar the Court had the roughly 65 lakh names left off the draft published booth by booth, with the reason for each, searchable by EPIC number and put up at panchayat and block offices. It allowed claims with a copy of Aadhaar and then made Aadhaar the twelfth document, as proof of identity. In West Bengal it let people flagged for discrepancies file through an authorised representative, gave them ten more days, and set up appellate tribunals of former judges for those whose claims judicial officers rejected. Its judgment of 27 May 2026 upheld the revision and said that people in Bihar wrongly deleted as absent, dead, shifted or duplicate may challenge the decision in court.
steps: Search the list of names left off by your EPIC number on the district or Chief Electoral Officer's website, or look at the panchayat or block notice board.
Note the reason given against your name. It tells you what to answer.
Aadhaar can be given as proof of identity. It is not accepted as proof of citizenship.
In West Bengal, a rejected claim goes to the appellate tribunal. A pending appeal did not give a right to vote at the 2026 poll.

sources.doc: Supreme Court order, 14.08.2025, W.P.(C) 640/2025, para 3(i)-(ii)
sources.quote: The list of 65,00,000 (approximate) voters, whose names appeared in the Voter List as on 2025 but are not included in the Draft Roll dated 01.08.2025, shall be ... displayed on the websites of the District Election Officers (District-wise). The information will be booth- wise, but it can be accessed by referring to the Electors Photo Identity Card (EPIC) number of each voter. (ii) The list so displayed shall also disclose the reason for non-inclusion in the Draft Roll.

sources.doc: Supreme Court order, 14.08.2025, para 3(vii)
sources.quote: In the public notice, it shall also be expressly mentioned that the aggrieved persons may submit their claims along with a copy of their Aadhar Card.

sources.doc: Supreme Court order, 08.09.2025, W.P.(C) 640/2025
sources.quote: Accordingly, we direct the Election Commission of India and its authorities to accept Aadhar Card as a proof of identity for the purpose of inclusion or exclusion in the revised voter list of the State of Bihar. Aadhaar Card, for this purpose, shall be treated as the 12th document by the Authorities.

sources.doc: Supreme Court order, 19.01.2026 (West Bengal), para 5(ii)
sources.quote: Persons likely to be affected are permitted to submit their documents/objections through their authorized representative. Such an authorised representative can even be a Booth Level Agent (BLA).

sources.doc: Supreme Court order, 10.03.2026 (West Bengal), paras 10-11
sources.quote: our order dated 24.02.2026, in no uncertain terms, points out that the orders passed by the judicial officers will not be subjected to appeal before any Executive/Administrative Officer.

sources.doc: Supreme Court order, 13.04.2026 (West Bengal), para 11
sources.quote: However, it goes without saying that the mere pendency of appeals preferred by excluded persons before the Appellate Tribunals shall not entitle them to exercise their right to vote.

sources.doc: Supreme Court judgment, ADR v. ECI, 2026 INSC 564, para 186(h)
sources.quote: all persons who are domiciled in Bihar and whose names have been erroneously deleted on the ground that they are absent, dead, shifted or in duplication may assail the decision of the Commission by way of judicial review.

sources.doc: Supreme Court judgment, ADR v. ECI, 2026 INSC 564, para 186(h)
sources.quote: In the event the Competent Authority holds that such deleted individuals are citizens, they shall be included in the electoral roll.

remedies.title: Going to court
remedies.plain: An elector can ask the High Court, under Article 226 of the Constitution, to review a decision on the roll. The Supreme Court's judgment of 27 May 2026 says the Commission's enquiry into eligibility remains open to judicial review, and that people in Bihar wrongly deleted as absent, dead, shifted or duplicate may challenge the decision that way. On 11 November 2025, while it was hearing the challenges to the revision, the Supreme Court asked the High Courts to hold back cases on whether the revision was valid. That request did not cover an elector's own case about his or her own entry. The judgment of 27 May 2026 decided the petitions about Bihar, and the petition in which the request was made is not among the cases it lists.
steps: Use the claim, the hearing and both appeals first, and keep every order.
If you still have no remedy, ask the District Legal Services Authority for a lawyer to file a writ petition in the High Court.

sources.doc: Supreme Court judgment, ADR v. ECI, 2026 INSC 564, para 175
sources.quote: Importantly, the entirety of this exercise remains amenable to judicial review, thereby ensuring that the enquiry is conducted in accordance with law and within the bounds of procedural fairness.

sources.doc: Supreme Court judgment, ADR v. ECI, 2026 INSC 564, para 186(h)
sources.quote: may assail the decision of the Commission by way of judicial review.

sources.doc: Supreme Court order of 11.11.2025 in W.P.(C) No. 1074/2025, as reproduced in the Supreme Court registry office report for 26.11.2025
sources.quote: Since this Court is seized of the matter pertaining to validity of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of Electoral Rolls in various States, including Bihar, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Pondicherry etc., we request the jurisdictional High Courts to keep in abeyance/defer the writ proceedings, if any, filed in those High Courts touching the validity of the SIR of electoral rolls in their respective States.

orgs.name: Citizens for Justice and Peace (CJP), Assam team
orgs.what: During the Special Revision, used community volunteers and local meetings to help electors facing objections, took a memorandum and a list of affected electors to the Election Commission, and intervened when ration dealers demanded documents.
orgs.source_outlet: CJP and Vote for Democracy training manual (own publication), p. 35
orgs.quote: Through our awareness meetings, unofficial connections, discussions with the BLOs in our network, and the dedication of our community volunteers, we were able to directly and indirectly assist hundreds of thousa nds of people.

orgs.name: SIR Sachetan Matadhikar Bachao Manch (SSMBM)
orgs.what: A forum formed at PUCL Chhattisgarh's call to deal with SIR problems. It trained volunteers, ran awareness meetings and took specific problems to the Chief Electoral Officer, who ordered forms filled wrongly by one BLO to be redone.
orgs.quote: Apart from meetings to train volunteers and spread awareness, the Forum also met with the CEO-Chhattisgarh to outline the problems people are facing.

orgs.name: Voter Adhikar Manch (VAM)
orgs.what: A citizens' collective of groups working with workers and migrants that ran helplines and physical help desks in working-class localities across Delhi, helping electors with progeny mapping and forms and taking their cases to the Chief Electoral Officer.
orgs.quote: We have assisted numerous people with progeny mapping, and the struggle to figure out the exact details of the polling booth in the exact assembly constituency that has been redrawn extensively in Delhi, where their parents would have voted 24 years ago, is harrowing.

orgs.name: Catholic Association of Goa, with the parish pastoral councils of the Church in Goa
orgs.what: During enumeration, parish pastoral council members were each put in charge of 35 to 40 households, visited them when the BLOs came, and checked the forms had been filled and the names kept on the roll. The councils said they would watch the draft roll's deletions and help get names restored.
orgs.quote: We were tasked to visit houses when the BLOs came and cross-check if they had done all the formalities properly and their names included in the roll.

orgs.name: My Vote, My Right Karnataka (MVMR-K)
orgs.what: A coalition that trained volunteers to run an SIR helpline and help desks in Bengaluru, mainly for migrants, slum dwellers, trans people, Muslims, Dalits and Adivasis, helping with the 2002 mapping and forms. It also took complaints to the Chief Electoral Officer.
orgs.source_outlet: BehanBox (first-person account by a helpline volunteer)
orgs.quote: Seeing how the process played out elsewhere, the MVMR-K coalition prepared by training volunteers like myself to run a helpline and help desks, particularly for communities at greater risk of being disenfranchised—migrants, slum dwellers, trans people, Muslims, Dalits, and Adivasis.

orgs.name: Solidarity Youth Movement (SYM), Haveri unit
orgs.what: Helped people in Haveri district trace their 2002 roll details for the enumeration form, through a WhatsApp group, and held workshops on what to do if a name is missing from the draft roll.
orgs.quote: the SYM had directly helped around 6,000 people in Haveri district, besides conducting awareness workshops on what to do if someone’s name is not on the draft rolls.

orgs.name: Diocese of Cochin (Roman Catholic)
orgs.what: After the SIR, began a door-to-door drive by trained youth volunteers to find people left off the roll or never enrolled among the diocese's 40,750 families in four Assembly constituencies, starting in one parish. Church leaders said at least 3,000 such people had been identified.
orgs.quote: At least 3,000 such people have already been identified during the drive, the Church leaders involved in the campaign said.

orgs.name: Edappally Mahallu Muslim Jama-ath committee, Kochi
orgs.what: Ran an SIR help desk during the revision, one of the earliest by the committee's own account. The Cochin Diocese later cited the Mahallu committees' help desks as the model for its own drive.
orgs.quote: the helpdesk that it set up, one of the earliest during the SIR, had turned out to be highly effective

orgs.name: Mosque committees of Balaramapuram town mosque and Chemboor mosque (Thiruvananthapuram), Panavally Thekkum Bhagam mosque (Alappuzha) and Badriya Masjid (Chavakkad, Thrissur)
orgs.what: Followed Vallakkadavu in setting up teams of volunteers to help the public complete the SIR enumeration form.
orgs.quote: Soon, several other committees - notable among them being Balaramapuram town mosque, Chemboor mosque in Thiruvananthapuram, Panavally Thekkum Bhagam mosque in Alappuzha and Badriya Masjid in Chavakkad -   followed suit and set up dedicated teams of volunteers to help the public complete the formality.

orgs.name: Vallakkadavu mosque (jamaath) committee, Thiruvananthapuram
orgs.what: Set up one of the first SIR help desks in Kerala in the first week of November 2025, open to the public as well as its own members, and filled in enumeration forms after finding people's names in the 2002 roll. Hundreds had used it within two weeks.
orgs.quote: It set up a help desk in the first week of November, urging mahal members as well as the public to seek its assistance in filling the enumeration form.

orgs.name: Citizens for Justice and Peace (CJP)
orgs.what: Ran SIR training and awareness sessions in Mumbai with community groups, covering documents, the 2002 roll linkage, notices, hearings and appeals.
orgs.quote: It is from this history of engagement that CJP, together with Vote for Democracy (VFD), began conducting a series of detailed SIR awareness and training sessions in Maharashtra.

orgs.name: Vote for Democracy (VFD)
orgs.what: Ran SIR training sessions in Maharashtra jointly with CJP and co-published a training manual on navigating enumeration, notices, hearings and appeals.
orgs.quote: It is from this history of engagement that CJP, together with Vote for Democracy (VFD), began conducting a series of detailed SIR awareness and training sessions in Maharashtra.

orgs.name: People's Union for Civil Liberties (PUCL), Rajasthan
orgs.what: Held form-filling camps with booth-level officers in Jaipur during enumeration and set up a response team for SIR problems across Rajasthan.
orgs.quote: Our performance was good, we helped fill and collected more than 300 to 400 forms in the camps that were organised.

orgs.name: Jamaat-e-Islami Hind, Coimbatore district unit
orgs.what: Ran SIR help camps on weekday evenings and full days at weekends in five Coimbatore localities (Podanur, Karumbukadai, GM Nagar, Saramedu and Kuniyamuthur) during enumeration.
orgs.quote: In Coimbatore, the Jamaat-e-Islami Hind is conducts camps in the evenings on week days and full-day camps on the weekend in Podanur, Karumbukadai, GM Nagar, Saramedu and Kuniyamuthur.

orgs.name: Tamil Nadu Thowheed Jamath (TNTJ), Tiruchy and Madurai units
orgs.what: Ran SIR help camps in at least 30 mosques in Tiruchy during enumeration. Volunteers searched the 2002 and 2005 rolls, checked people's details and helped them fill their forms. The Madurai branches trained office-bearers across 36 units.
orgs.quote: In Tiruchy, Tamil Nadu Thowheed Jamath (TNTJ) has set up camps in at least 30 mosques. Volunteers, who have downloaded PDFs of the 2002 and 2005 voter rolls, entered the details into Excel sheets, verify data and help people in filling SIR forms.

orgs.name: All India Peoples Mission
orgs.what: Among the church bodies that organised help desks in Hyderabad to help voters complete enumeration forms.
orgs.quote: The Catholic Archdiocese of Hyderabad, All India Peoples Mission and the Telangana Council of Churches were among those organising the help desks.

orgs.name: Catholic Archdiocese of Hyderabad
orgs.what: Among the church bodies that set up help desks across Hyderabad, staffed by trained volunteers, to help voters complete enumeration forms.
orgs.quote: The Catholic Archdiocese of Hyderabad, All India Peoples Mission and the Telangana Council of Churches were among those organising the help desks.

orgs.name: Masjid-e-Teenposh and Imdadul Uloom Madrasa, Red Hills, Hyderabad

orgs.name: Telangana Council of Churches
orgs.what: Among the church bodies that organised help desks in Hyderabad to help voters complete enumeration forms.
orgs.quote: The Catholic Archdiocese of Hyderabad, All India Peoples Mission and the Telangana Council of Churches were among those organising the help desks.

orgs.what: Held camps in Muslim-majority areas during enumeration to explain the forms and documents, about 500 a day by its own count.
orgs.quote: The All Bengal Minority Youth Federation, one of the largest organisations in the community, has also swung into action.

orgs.name: Dinajpur Notun Alo
orgs.what: A community organisation of trans people in Uttar Dinajpur that said it had been focused on the SIR and on supporting its community through it, though that work had slowed by April 2026.

orgs.what: Held daily training sessions and help desks at the mosque to guide people through the enumeration form.
orgs.quote: The Nakhoda Masjid and several other major mosques have begun holding daily training sessions outside prayer halls and conducting help desks to guide people through the SIR process

orgs.name: Society for Human Development and Social Action
orgs.what: Worked for sex workers in Kolkata alongside two other NGOs during the revision. It had urged the Chief Electoral Officer's office to reach these women, welcomed the assistance camps held in red-light areas, and asked the Commission to accept documents issued by their cooperative society.
orgs.quote: NGO representatives said a total of more than 300 women turned up across three camps in Chetla, Kidderpore and Kalighat during the day.

orgs.name: United Medicos
orgs.what: Worked with a partner organisation on a team that drafted appeals for electors removed from the roll and filed them online, or on paper for those who could not use the portal.
